# tools/gates/fmt-baseline.txt -- the files `cargo fmt --all --check` still finds,
# and who owes each one. Read by `tools/gate fmt`.
#
# THIS LIST ONLY SHRINKS. A file here is one somebody must reformat; a file NOT
# here that rustfmt disagrees with fails the gate. Both directions fail, which
# is the same ratchet COVERAGE.md runs for generated files: the count moves when
# a person looks at it and decides, never on its own.
#
# Why it is not empty, since a fmt baseline is a strange thing to need. Until
# 6e50a185 this tree had no rustfmt.toml, so `cargo fmt` and `tools/lane.sh fmt`
# formatted the same file differently and neither answer was wrong -- there was
# no answer. 50 files had drifted by the time one was written. 874e6c34
# canonicalised the 31 that no live lane was holding. These 19 are the rest, and
# every one is either dirty in the shared tree right now or inside a lane's
# declared territory: reformatting a file somebody is mid-edit in destroys their
# work, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed.
#
# TO CLEAR YOUR LINE: `tools/lane.sh fmt <file>` (or --allow-root for a lib.rs,
# and then check what else it reflowed -- rustfmt follows `mod`), delete the
# line, commit both together. The gate fails on a line that is no longer true,
# so a stale entry cannot sit here looking like work.
#
# Nothing may be added here to make a red gate green. A NEW unformatted file
# means run rustfmt, not edit this file. The only admissible reason for a new
# line is the one every line below carries: another lane owns that file right
# now and this is a handoff, not an exemption.

# --- Structured lane -------------------------------------------------------
crates/dclutch-product/tests/payoff__basis_corpus_v3.rs
crates/dclutch-rational-open-wasm/src/wire.rs

# --- Dealer lane -----------------------------------------------------------
# dclutch-trading is the ONE package that declares edition 2021, so these
# are the files the two formatters disagreed about most sharply. They are now
# 2024-style everywhere; these four just have not been run through it yet.

# --- Direct lane -----------------------------------------------------------

# --- Redemption lane -------------------------------------------------------

# --- The fold of 2026-09-05 (WORKSPACE-ONE) --------------------------------
# These 126 files are not new drift. Until 2026-09-05 the tree was 55 Cargo
# workspaces and `cargo fmt --all` reached only the 41 members of the root one,
# so `tools/gate fmt` had never once looked at a program-test suite, a gauntlet
# campaign or the successor. Folding the tree into one workspace did not change
# a byte of any of them; it changed what the gate can see.
#
# They are a HANDOFF, not an exemption, and the admissible reason this file
# names is the one they carry: two lanes are live in this territory (SUITES-
# REPAIR in the program-test suites, WEB-REDS in apps/ and packages/) and
# several of these files are dirty in the shared tree as this is written.
# Reformatting them under a live repair lane destroys work to fix whitespace.
# Whoever next owns an area below clears its lines with it.
#
# Rows are the NORMALISED path: a `#[path]`-linked successor module is one
# file here however many campaigns compile it.
#
# The whole block is owed. It is the largest single debt in this file and it
# should be the shortest-lived.
